newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money eases on improved liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money eases on improved liquidity.

text.p: Indian call money rates were quoted at 1.00-1.50 percent in latest trade on Wednesday, down from the day's opening levels of 1.75-2.00 and the previous close of 2.25-3.00 percent, dealers said.
The easy money conditions and covered positions ahead of reporting Friday will keep the call market dull, inactive and at lower levels, a dealer said.
"The rate may go below 1.0 percent today," he said.

There is an inflow in excess of 40.0 billion rupees in the first fortnight of June and the only expected major outflow is on account of advance tax payment to the tune of 20.0 billion rupees, Ashish Pitale at ICICI securities and Finance said.
The ease in call money rates will push the securities yields down, a dealer said. "The market is expected to see a good volume trading today," he said.
